sentences.text: In view of the recommendation letter dated 26.07.2016, Respondent No. 2 is deleted from the array of parties.

5. List on 04.09.2023.
CM APPL. 24029/2023 (application filed under Order 22 Rule 3 CPC) by legal heirs of late Mrs.
Sheela, daughter of late Mr. Bhagwan)
6.
The original Petitioner, late Sh. Bhagwan has expired on 07.05.2022.
The present application has been filed by the children of his pre-deceased daughter late Ms. Sheela.

The name of the grandchildren, who are the applicants is (i) Mr. Akshay Dabas; and (ii) Mr. Deepak Dabas and they are seeking leave to be impleaded as legal heirs of the Petitioner in the present petition.
7. A separate application CM No. 31304/2022 has been filed by the four sons of late Sh. Bhagwan seeking their impleadment to the exclusion of their sisters and their legal heirs.

The counsel, Mr.
Rajesh Dabas, appearing for the applicants in CM No. 31304/2022 has opposed this application.
8. Notice in this application was issued on 27.03.2023.
9. Mr. Rajesh Dabas, Advocate, for the legal heirs CM No. 31304/2022 accepts notice.
He states that he does not wish to file any reply to this application and is willing to address arguments.
He states that daughters of late Mr. Bhagwan are not entitled to be impleaded in view of the provisions of Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 ('DLR Act').

He states that the devolution of interest shall be in accordance with Section 50 (a) of the DLR Act, where under the sons of late Mr. Bhagwan are entitled to succeed to the exclusion of his daughters.
He states that the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 ('Act of This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 09:16:34 1956') will have no application and in this regard, he relies upon the judgment of Har Naraini Devi &
Anr. v. Union of India, (2022) 13 Scale 624 (paragraphs 25 and 26).

sentences.text: 10. In response, learned counsel for Respondent, DDA states that the acquisition proceeding of the land holding of late Mr. Bhagwan stood completed during his lifetime.
The compensation and solatium in lieu of acquisition were also received by him under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. 10.1.
He states therefore the applicability provision of DLR Act does not arise in the facts of this case.

He states that the subject matter of the present matter is the allotment of alternate land to late Mr.
Bhagwan, which claim arises on account of rehabilitation measures proposed by DDA under an administrative scheme.
He states that the right to allotment of the said alternate plot does not attract the provisions of DLR Act and would be governed by the Act of 1956.
11. This Court has considered the submissions of the counsel appearing for applicants in CM APPL.

sentences.text: The applicants in CM APPL No. 31304/2022 are the four sons of late Mr. Bhagwan.
In the said application, the said four sons have relied upon a will dated 29.09.2014, purported to have executed by late Mr. Bhagwan to assert that the right to suit have survived on them.
It is stated in the said application that the daughter of late Mr. Bhagwan were excluded from claiming any interest in the said alternate plot.
There is no reference in this application to the provisions of the DLR Act.

13. This Court finds merits in the submission of learned counsel for DDA that the subject matter of the present contempt petition is the allotment of the alternative plot to late Mr. Bhagwan which is admittedly not an agricultural This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 09:16:35 holding.
In this view of matter, the provisions of DLR Act would have no application to the alternate plot, which would be governed by the general laws including the Act of 1956.
The DLR Act is a special law which deals with rights over agricultural holdings, whereas the alternate plot which is a subject matter of this petitions is not an agricultural holding.
14. The legal heirs of late Smt. Sheela have not admitted the veracity and validity of the will dated 29.09.2014.

15. This Court has also perused the judgment in Har Naraini Devi (supra), wherein Supreme Court at paragraph 25 has categorically observed that the effect of the deletion of Section 4 (2) of the Act of 1956 is prospective and the said deletion can only be in respect of successions which open on or after 09.09.2015.
In the present case, late Mr. Bhagwan expired on 07.05.2022 i.e., much after the deletion of 4 (2) of the Act of 1956.
16. In these facts and circumstances, this application is allowed and the applicant herein are impleaded as Petitioners in their capacity as the legal heirs of late Mr. Bhagwan.
17. This is an application filed seeking condonation of delay of 16 days in re-filing CM APPL 24029/2023.
The said application is not opposed.
18. The delay is condoned and the application is allowed.

19. This is an application filed seeking condonation of delay of 230 days in filing CM APPL.
24029/2023.
This application is not opposed.
No arguments have been addressed.
20. The delay is condoned and the application is allowed.

sentences.text: This is an application filed by the four sons of late Mr. Bhagwan seeking their impleadment to the exclusion of their three sisters by relying upon a Will dated 29.09.2014, stated to have been executed by late Mr. Bhagwan.
The name of the three daughters is Mrs. Annu, late Mrs. Nirmala and late Mrs. Sheela.

22. As noted above legal heirs of late Mrs. Sheela, one of the sisters has not admitted to the validity of the will dated 29.09.2014. The applicants i.e., the four sons have not filed a no objection certificate of Mrs. Annu and the legal heirs of late Mrs. Nirmala.
23.

In the facts of this case, it is directed that all the four sons, Mrs. Annu, legal heirs of late Mrs.
Nirmala and legal heirs of late Mrs. Sheela are entitled to be brought on record as the natural legal heirs of late Mr. Bhagwan.
24. Accordingly, the applicant herein is directed to file a memo of parties bringing all the said legal heirs on record.
25. The amended memo of parties be filed within a period of two (2) weeks.
26. With the aforesaid directions, the present application is disposed of.
MANMEET PRITAM SINGH ARORA, J MAY 15, 2023/
